Calculate the Randomness Ratio of a Time Series

Source: R/randomness_ratio_loess.R
randomness_ratio_loess.Rd

Fits a generalized additive model (GAM) with a smooth function of time to capture linear and nonlinear temporal patterns. The randomness ratio is calculated as the variance of the residuals divided by the variance of the original observations.

randomness_ratio_loess(y, k = 10)

Arguments

y

A numeric vector containing the time series observations.

k

An integer specifying the basis dimension for the smooth term. The default is 10. Larger values allow more complex fitted shapes, subject to the smoothing penalty and available data.

Value

A numeric value representing the randomness ratio: $$\frac{\operatorname{Var}(y_t - \hat{f}(t))} {\operatorname{Var}(y_t)}$$ where \(\hat{f}(t)\) is the fitted smooth function of time.

Details

A low randomness ratio indicates that a large proportion of the variation is explained by the fitted smooth trend. A high ratio indicates that more variation remains unexplained by the fitted model.

The function uses mgcv::gam() with a penalized smooth term, s(t), and selects the smoothing parameter using restricted maximum likelihood (method = "REML").

The ratio is not necessarily bounded by zero and one because the residual variance and original variance are calculated separately. Its value depends on the smoothness of the fitted model and the characteristics of the time series.

References

Wood, S. N. (2017). Generalized Additive Models: An Introduction with R (2nd ed.). Chapman and Hall/CRC.

See also

mgcv::gam(), mgcv::s()
